newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan parliament passes deficit budget.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan parliament passes deficit budget.

text.p: The Moroccan parliament on Sunday passed a 12.4 billion dirham ($1.3 billion) deficit budget for 1997/98.

The official Moroccan news agency MAP said the finance law was adopted by 54 votes to 41 against. MAP gave no other details but a member of parliament told Reuters the draft had been passed with no major change.
Under the draft outlined by Finance Minister Mohammed Kabbaj last month spending will total around 126.7 billion dirhams compared with 117.1 billion dirhams in 1996/97.
Revenue for fiscal 1997/98 was put at 114.3 billion dirhams compared with 107.7 in the previous fiscal year.
Presenting his draft, Kabbaj forecast the economy would grow "up to 2.0 to 3.0 percent this year and strong growth in 1998".

Kabbaj forecast a rise in phosphates and by-products exports and improvement of tourism receipts and remittances of Moroccan expatriates. But agriculture output was expected to drop 30 percent compared with the previous year because of changes in the weather.
Agriculture represents nearly 20 percent of Morocco's GDP and employs nearly 50 percent of the country's estimated 10 million workforce.
In the 1995/96 agriculture season Morocco harvest 10 million tonnes of cereals against 1.6 million the season before which was badly affected by drought.

During debate last week, MAP quoted Mohamed Kemmou, leader of the pro-government Constitutional Union party, as saying the budget "strives for the promotion of the private sector and reinforcement of competitiveness, as well as to encourage private initiatives and continued reform in the productive sectors".
Opposition party spokesman Fathallah Oualaalou told parliament that this year would see "negative" economic growth which could not be blamed solely on climate.

The leader of the opposition Socialist Union of People's Forces said the finance law was a "mirror reflecting the economic crisis affecting the country" as a result of "inappropriate options and bad management".
